**No confirmed price changes since Monday for the four I could read. Close is the one that matters, because its $9 plan is now single-user.** I can't tell when any of these pages last changed. My Monday answer is the only baseline, and it was per seat per month, billed annually.

- **HubSpot Sales Hub:** unchanged as checked. Starter still lists $20/seat/mo, with a $7 figure beside it that is discounted and for new customers only [R17]. The page doesn't make clear which billing period each figure belongs to. A Nov 10 post mentions a new pricing model this year, but I couldn't date it [R21].
- **Pipedrive:** unchanged as checked. The $14 per seat per month billed annually plan is now called "Lite", and I had called it Essential [R12]. A Pipedrive MCP skills page dated Nov 10 exists, but I couldn't tell whether it is new [R4].
- **Zoho CRM:** couldn't verify. The pricing page loaded but showed no figures, so I can't confirm the $14 for Standard [R11]. My news search found nothing relevant.
- **Salesforce:** unchanged as checked. Pro Suite is $100/user/mo billed annually [R13]. Quick Pages (beta) was announced Nov 5, before Monday [R6].
- **Close:** changed. There is no "Startup" plan any more. The $9 plan is Solo and is limited to 1 user [R14]. For 20 people the entry plan is Essentials at $35, shown next to $49 [R14]. The page doesn't say which figure is the annual one.

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for all five. I also ran one news search per vendor dated from Nov 9. The no-change findings mean no change found in what I checked.

Couldn't verify: $14 (cited R11)

You asked on 3 November: "Which managed Postgres host has the cheapest entry paid plan?" My answer was Neon Launch at $5/month, Supabase Pro at $25/month and Render Postgres from $6/month. That answer is partly out of date. The Neon figure no longer matches its pricing page.

- **Neon Launch:** I said $5/month. The live page now shows usage-based pricing, with $0.106 per CU-hour and $0.35 per GB-month, and a "typical spend" of $15/mo. It shows no $5 flat price [R8]. **Changed.** I can't tell when it changed. The $5 I found is for AI Gateway credits, not the plan [R17].
- **Supabase Pro:** I said $25/month. The page still shows $25/month, which includes $10 of compute credit [R6]. **Unchanged as checked.**
- **Render Postgres:** I said from $6/month. The page still lists $6/month for the smallest paid instance (256 MB RAM) [R7]. **Unchanged as checked.**

Render is now the cheapest entry paid plan I can confirm. Neon has no fixed entry price to compare against.

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for Neon, Supabase and Render. I also ran one news search per vendor for changes since 3 November. I found no Supabase or Render pricing change in what I checked.

As of 2026-11-11 12:58 (Asia/Kolkata), Wednesday

Of the four prices I gave you on 2026-11-03, one no longer matches, two are unchanged as checked, and one I couldn't verify on AWS's own page. You said "last Tuesday", which could mean 11-03 or 11-10. I used 11-03, the date of my earlier answer.

- **Neon Launch:** my earlier answer said it starts at $5/month. The live page now shows Launch as usage-based, at $0.106 per CU-hour and $0.35 per GB-month, with a "typical spend" of $15/mo. It shows no $5 minimum [R16]. Verdict: **changed**. I can't tell whether Neon changed this after 11-03 or my $5 figure was wrong.
- **Supabase Pro:** earlier $25/month. The live page still shows $25/month, with $10 of compute credits included [R17]. Verdict: **unchanged as checked**.
- **Render Postgres:** earlier from $6/month. The live page still lists $6/month for the smallest paid instance (256 MB) [R19]. Verdict: **unchanged as checked**.
- **AWS RDS db.t4g.micro:** earlier about $12/month. The official page I read shows no instance prices [R18]. A third-party page lists $0.016/hour single-AZ [R20]. By my own calculation, $0.016 × 730 hours is about $11.68/month. Verdict: **couldn't verify** on AWS's own page.

Checked: live pages for Neon, Supabase, Render and AWS RDS PostgreSQL pricing. One news search per vendor since 2026-11-03. I found no other price changes in what I checked.

Render Postgres's cheapest paid instance is $6/month, which is about ₹571/month at 95.22 INR per USD. I got that by multiplying 6 × 95.22. The rate is an Xe mid-market quote dated 2026-10-28, not a live one [R2]. Another converter showed about 95.01, which would give about ₹570 [R4]. Your bank or card rate will differ. I didn't see anything saying Render bills in INR, so you'd probably be charged in USD and converted.

- **Instance price:** $6/month for 256 MB RAM and 1 GB of storage. This is unchanged from my earlier answer. I read Render's pricing page live today [R1].
- **Workspace fee:** my earlier answer said a $25/mo Pro workspace might be required. The page also lists a Hobby workspace at $0/mo plus compute [R1]. So the $6 likely applies on Hobby. I couldn't confirm that Hobby allows paid databases. Verdict: changed (my earlier caveat is now less likely to matter).
- **Extra storage:** $0.30/GB beyond the included 1 GB [R1].
